rules.description: Special Leave Petition (Civil) under Article 136 against a civil judgment, decree, determination or order. Cause title or cover says SLP (C), SLP (Civil), or Special Leave Petition (Civil). Not a civil appeal, writ, review, or miscellaneous application.

Special Leave Petition (Criminal) under Article 136 in a criminal proceeding. Cause title or cover says SLP (Crl.), SLP (Criminal), or Special Leave Petition (Criminal). Not a criminal appeal, writ, or review.
Civil Appeal to the Supreme Court of India, including an appeal by High Court certificate or an armed forces tribunal civil appeal. Cause title or cover says Civil Appeal or C.A. Not an SLP (Civil).
Criminal Appeal to the Supreme Court of India. Cause title or cover says Criminal Appeal or Crl.A. Not an SLP (Criminal).
Writ Petition (Civil) under Article 32 of the Constitution for enforcement of fundamental or other civil rights. Cause title or cover says Writ Petition (Civil) or W.P.(C).
Writ Petition (Criminal) under Article 32 involving personal liberty or a criminal matter. Cause title or cover says Writ Petition (Criminal) or W.P.(Crl.).

Transfer Petition (Civil) seeking transfer of a civil case from one High Court or court to another, typically under Article 139A of the Constitution or Section 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Cause title or cover says Transfer Petition (Civil) or T.P.(C).

Transfer Petition (Criminal) seeking transfer of a criminal case from one court to another, typically under Section 406 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Cause title or cover says Transfer Petition (Criminal) or T.P.(Crl.).
Review Petition (Civil) under Article 137 seeking review of a Supreme Court civil judgment. Cause title or cover says Review Petition (Civil) or R.P.(C). Not a curative petition.
Review Petition (Criminal) under Article 137 seeking review of a Supreme Court criminal judgment. Cause title or cover says Review Petition (Criminal) or R.P.(Crl.). Not a curative petition.
Original Suit in the Supreme Court under Article 131, typically a dispute between the Union and a State or between States. Cause title or cover says Original Suit or O.S.
Contempt Petition (Civil) for civil contempt of the Supreme Court or of its orders. Cause title or cover says Contempt Petition (Civil) or Cont.P.(C).
Contempt Petition (Criminal) for criminal contempt of the Supreme Court. Cause title or cover says Contempt Petition (Criminal) or Cont.P.(Crl.).
Election Petition in the Supreme Court, including a Presidential or Vice-Presidential election petition. Cause title or cover says Election Petition.

Arbitration Petition in the Supreme Court under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, typically for appointment of an arbitrator or a related arbitration proceeding. Cause title or cover says Arbitration Petition or Arb.P.
Curative Petition (Civil) filed after dismissal of a review petition in a civil matter. Cause title or cover says Curative Petition (Civil). Not a review petition.
Curative Petition (Criminal) filed after dismissal of a review petition in a criminal matter. Cause title or cover says Curative Petition (Criminal). Not a review petition.

Miscellaneous Application (M.A.) or Interlocutory Application (I.A.) in a pending Supreme Court matter, including restoration, clarification, modification, listing, or a similar application. Cause title or cover says M.A., I.A., Miscellaneous Application, or Interlocutory Application. Not a fresh SLP, appeal, writ, review, or curative petition.

court.description: Court where the petition is filed, as a string. Fill from Cover Page; check spelling on Main Petition and Vakalatnama.

petition_type.description: Petition type as printed, e.g. Special Leave Petition (Civil) or Transfer Petition (Civil). Fill from the Main Petition cause title first. If not printed there, fill from the Cover Page cause title. Check spelling against the other.

cause_title.description: Cause title representing petitioner vs respondent. Fill from Cover Page. If Cover Page is not in this pack, fill from the Main Petition caption and draft formatted_title from party counts.

advocates_on_record.description: Printed AOR footer only. Leave a field null if it is not printed; do not invent name, code, email, mobile, firm, chamber, or PIN. Do not copy petitioner or respondent names or addresses. Prefer Vakalatnama. If Vakalatnama is not in this pack or prints no AOR, use the Memo of Appearance footer, then the last page of the Main Petition (very end: Drawn By, Filed on, DRAWN & FILED BY, Advocate for Petitioner/Respondent, Chamber lines under the name). Do not use Main Petition opening or party-list pages. If office_address is still blank, last page of Listing Proforma / Proforma for First Listing. Remaining blanks: AOR's Certificate signature / DRAWN & FILED BY and Advocate's Checklist. Never override Vakalatnama.
advocates_on_record.title: Advocates On Record

impugned_orders.description: Primary impugned order only. Fill from the Impugned Order PDF if it is in this pack. If it is not attached, fill from bracketed particulars on the Main Petition cause title, Cover Page, AOR's Certificate, and Affidavit. If the same order appears in several of those, keep the Impugned Order PDF values when present; otherwise keep one consistent set and record mismatches in inconsistencies.
impugned_orders.title: Impugned Orders

relief_sort.description: Main prayer body only from the Main Petition last 2-3 pages. Copy the text under the heading Main Prayer or Prayer. Do not include the heading, clause number, markdown, or HTML (for example omit '7. MAIN PRAYER:' and '<u>**MAIN PRAYER**</u>:'). Start at the prayer sentence, e.g. 'In the circumstances stated above…'. Leave null if that heading is not printed.
relief_sort.title: Relief Sort

petition_date.description: Date of this petition from the last page of the Main Petition, after the heading Main Prayer or Prayer. Use the date printed next to Date, Date Drafted, or Date Filed on. If both Date Drafted and Date Filed on are printed, use only the Date Drafted date. Return the date as printed, without the label. Do not use a date inside the prayer, an impugned-order date, or a date from any other document. Leave null if none of those labels is printed after the prayer.
petition_date.title: Petition Date

inconsistencies.description: Spelling mismatches between fill and verify sources, plus an ORGANIZATION party with no acting_through. Always include a letter-level mismatch of the Cause Title main petitioner or main respondent versus petitioner 1 / respondent 1 on the Main Petition starting pages (e.g. Shalija vs Shailja). Cover Page has only one name per side; extra parties continue on later starting pages. Also flag when that Cause Title person is missing on those pages, is a different person than petitioner 1 / respondent 1, or is listed on the other side. Extra parties are not a mismatch against Cover Page And Anr/Ors. Also record Impugned Order case number, date, or forum mismatches across Impugned Order, Main Petition, Cover Page, AOR's Certificate, and Affidavit. Also record printed AOR chamber/office address mismatches across Vakalatnama, Memo of Appearance, Main Petition last page, Listing Proforma last page, and AOR's Certificate. Quote both printed strings. Do not invent an address. Ignore extra Ph. on the same chamber line. Party-name items[].raw_text is Cause Title: "Name"; Main Petition: "Name". items[].id is '1', '2', ….

data_schema.title: LegalExtractRecord

categories.name: Advocate's Checklist
categories.description:
IDENTITY: The independent advocate/AOR filing-compliance checklist for the current Supreme Court filing, regardless of proceeding type.
START: CHECK LIST, CHECKLIST, CHECK-LIST or a clear OCR variant, supported by numbered compliance questions and YES/NO/N.A. responses about limitation, fees, copies or certification.
CONTINUE: Include all questions, continuation sheets and the checklist's own compliance declaration, date and AOR signature/details.
END: Before the next independently established outer document; do not require a signature to be present.
DO NOT SPLIT: Closing declarations/certificates remain in this checklist. A registry, government or lower-court checklist reproduced in another document keeps that enclosing category.
REPEAT: A separately presented checklist starts a new segment; continued questions do not.

categories.name: Cover Page
categories.description:
IDENTITY: The outer title sheet introducing the current Supreme Court paper book or an independently presented volume.
START: Court, jurisdiction, case/parties and filing-advocate details in a cover-sheet layout, corroborated by PAPER BOOK, COVER PAGE, For Index Please See Inside, or the surrounding bundle/volume opening.
CONTINUE: Include integral cover continuation only.
END: Before the first actual contents table, form, pleading or other independent document.
DO NOT SPLIT: A Supreme Court caption alone is insufficient. Dedicated opening/title pages of Main Petition, Application, Affidavit or another form belong to that document. A reproduced lower-court cover stays with its enclosing record.
REPEAT: Each independently established volume cover starts a new segment.

categories.name: Record of Proceedings
categories.description:
IDENTITY: An independent Supreme Court hearing/proceedings record for the current case, or the current paper book's outer Record of Proceedings register.
START: RECORD OF PROCEEDING(S) or a clear OCR variant, supported by hearing dates, appearances, directions or orders. A blank register with serial/date/pages columns also qualifies when its position and surrounding current-filing documents establish its outer role; it need not repeat a Supreme Court caption.
CONTINUE: Keep the complete record, appearances, order text, signatures and captionless continuation pages; no fixed page count is required.
END: Before the next independent hearing record or other outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: Lower-court connected-case captions, counsel lists and 'having come up for hearing' or 'delivered the following' wording within a judgment are not outer Record of Proceedings. Historical Supreme Court records and all records reproduced inside an Annexure stay with that Annexure even if headed RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS. ORDER within an established record does not make it Impugned Order. A petitioner-prepared chronology is List of Dates & Events.
REPEAT: A separately presented current-case hearing record starts a new segment, even adjacent to another record.

categories.name: AOR's Declaration
categories.description:
IDENTITY: An independent AOR/advocate declaration about curing or refiling defects in the current Supreme Court filing.
START: DECLARATION, DECLEARTION, DECLERATION or a clear variant, with statements that defects were cured, changes are confined to curing defects, or paper books are complete.
CONTINUE: Include the declaration body, date, signature and contact details.
END: Before the next independently established outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: A declaration within Main Petition, Advocate's Checklist or Listing Proforma stays there. A sworn statement is evaluated as Affidavit; a pleadings-confined certification as AOR's Certificate.
REPEAT: A separately presented declaration starts a new segment; signature continuation does not.

categories.name: AOR's Certificate
categories.description:
IDENTITY: An independent AOR filing certificate for the current Supreme Court proceeding.
START: CERTIFICATE or a clear OCR/letter-spaced variant, with certification that the primary pleading is confined to pleadings/documents before the challenged court/authority, or equivalent filing-certification language. Confirm current case context without a fixed heading position.
CONTINUE: Include its complete certification, filing date, signature and advocate details.
END: Before the next independently established outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: A signature block alone is insufficient. Certificates inside Checklist, Listing Proforma, Annexure, Appendix or another document remain there. Defect-curing declarations are AOR's Declaration.
REPEAT: A separately presented certificate starts a new segment.

categories.name: Index
categories.description:
IDENTITY: An independent contents index for the current Supreme Court paper book or volume.
START: A structured document/particulars list or table with printed page/folio references, usually headed INDEX or a clear variant.
CONTINUE: Keep the whole table, unheaded continuation pages, wrapped rows and associated entries.
END: Before an actual independently established document or a new volume's separate index; an item listed in a row is not that document's start.
DO NOT SPLIT: Determine function: a contents table titled FILING INDEX is Index; a submission memo identifying papers being tendered and advocate/date is Filing Memo. Internal indexes in reproduced records stay with those records.
REPEAT: A separate master/volume index starts a new segment; continuation of the same table does not.

categories.name: Office Report on Limitation
categories.description:
IDENTITY: The independent Supreme Court Registry limitation report for the current filing.
START: OFFICE REPORT ON LIMITATION, O/R ON LIMITATION or a clear OCR variant, supported by filing/refiling timeliness or delay fields.
CONTINUE: Include all report fields, continuation and registry certification.
END: Before the next independently established outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: Ordinary limitation discussion and condonation-of-delay applications do not qualify. REPORT OF FRESH CASE, OFFICE REPORT OF FRESH CASE and FRESH CASE REPORT are not this category merely because they discuss limitation. A report reproduced inside an exhibit stays there.
REPEAT: Only a separate qualifying report starts another segment; never invent a missing report.

categories.name: Listing Proforma
categories.description:
IDENTITY: The independent first-listing information form for the current Supreme Court filing.
START: PROFORMA/PERFORMA, PRO FORMA, LISTING PROFORMA/PERFORMA, PROFORMA/PERFORMA FOR FIRST LISTING, PROFORMA OF FIRST LISTING, LISTED PROFORMA or a clear variant, supported by prompt/value fields about Acts/sections, challenged court/order/date, judges, nature of matter, parties or related cases.
CONTINUE: Keep all continuation fields, closing date, AOR code, advocate details, declaration/certificate and signature, even without a repeated heading.
END: Before the next independently established outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: Bare PROFORMA without listing context is insufficient. Its closing advocate details are not AOR's Certificate. A similar form reproduced inside a record keeps that enclosing category.
REPEAT: A separately presented first-listing form starts a new segment.

categories.name: Synopsis
categories.description:
IDENTITY: The current filing's narrative summary of the dispute, issues and reasons for relief.
START: SYNOPSIS or a clear OCR variant with narrative summary content. Under a combined SYNOPSIS AND LIST OF DATES heading, narrative pages belong here.
CONTINUE: Keep narrative continuations, quotations of judgments and document references.
END: Before a separately introduced LIST OF DATES / LIST OF DATES AND EVENTS / LIST OF EVENTS chronology or the next independent outer document. Apply the shared-page rule when both start on one page.
DO NOT SPLIT: Ordinary dates, annexure references and quoted headings in narrative do not create boundaries. A synopsis reproduced in a lower-court record stays with that record.
REPEAT: Only a separately established outer synopsis starts another segment.

categories.name: List of Dates & Events
categories.description:
IDENTITY: The current filing's independent chronological account of dates and events.
START: LIST OF DATES, LIST OF DATES AND EVENTS, LIST OF DATES & EVENTS, LIST OF EVENTS or a clear variant, with a sequence of dates/date ranges linked to events. A combined SYNOPSIS AND LIST OF DATES heading belongs here when the page is chronological.
CONTINUE: Include complete date/event rows, wrapped descriptions, quotations and unheaded continuations; each page need not repeat a date. Dates may be full or partial.
END: Before the next independently established outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: Annexure references or quoted passages stay in the chronology. Narrative Synopsis and court-generated Record of Proceedings are different categories. A chronology within a reproduced record stays there.
REPEAT: Only a separately established outer chronology starts another segment.

categories.name: Main Petition
categories.description:
IDENTITY: The primary substantive pleading for the current Supreme Court proceeding: SLP, Writ Petition, Civil/Criminal Appeal, Transfer, Review, Curative, Arbitration or Contempt Petition, Original Suit or another supported main proceeding.
START: Its own opening/title and party block, linked to substantive facts, questions of law, grounds, declarations or prayers. Include dedicated opening pages even when the body starts later; a matching court caption alone is insufficient.
CONTINUE: Keep all pleadings through prayer, integral verification, drafting/filing dates and advocate details. Captionless continuations retain this identity once their current-pleading ownership is established.
END: Before a separately introduced AOR's Certificate, primary supporting Affidavit or another independent outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: Internal grounds, declarations, prayers, quotations and annexure references are not new documents. Do not require SLP-specific Form 28, a populated case number or one fixed format. Incidental I.A.s are Application. Earlier/lower-court pleadings reproduced in a record stay with that record, including petitions/appeals. Historical Supreme Court pleadings inside an Annexure also stay enclosed, even with a full petition title, matching parties or Supreme Court caption; they are not the current Main Petition.
REPEAT: Only a separately established current primary pleading starts another segment.

categories.name: Affidavit
categories.description:
IDENTITY: The independent primary pleading's affidavit in the current Supreme Court filing.
START: AFFIDAVIT or a clear OCR/letter-spaced variant with sworn statements and deponent, verification or oath/notarial features. Its stated purpose and current case context must support the current primary pleading, not an earlier proceeding or incidental application.
CONTINUE: Keep all sworn statements, verification, signatures and attestation pages, including captionless continuations.
END: Before the next independently established outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: Party names or an AFFIDAVIT heading alone are insufficient. An affidavit expressly verifying an Application stays with that Application, even if separately headed or Supreme Court-captioned. Lower-court affidavits and historical Supreme Court affidavits reproduced inside an Annexure stay enclosed, even with a matching heading or the same parties. Unsworn AOR certificates/declarations are not Affidavit; missing attestation alone does not disqualify an otherwise established affidavit.
REPEAT: A separate current primary-supporting affidavit starts a new segment.

categories.name: Annexures
categories.description:
IDENTITY: Each independent outer supporting exhibit of the current Supreme Court paper book.
START: An actual exhibit opening, supported either by an outer annexure label with a separate cover, matched Index/folio range, source transition/certification or outer folio transition; or, if the label is absent/unreadable, by a matched outer Index range and the actual indexed source opening. A label or Index mention alone is insufficient. An outer ANNEXURE P/n heading with a new notice, letter or order's own issuer/date establishes a new exhibit even when the preceding segment is also Annexures.
CONTINUE: Keep the complete exhibit as one segment, including cover, translations, certification and reproduced records.
END: Before the next corroborated outer exhibit or independent outer document, never at a guessed label.
DO NOT SPLIT: ANNEXURE P-7, ANNEXURE-P/7 or TRUE COPY inside an ongoing Synopsis, chronology, petition, Application, Index row, Affidavit, order or Appendix is not a boundary. Internal petitions, indexes, affidavits, orders, case-specific APPENDIX OF WP(C) exhibit lists and local ANNEXURE NO. 1 labels stay enclosed; narrative/table/numbering continuity takes precedence over an unsupported heading.
REPEAT: Each genuinely separate exhibit starts a new segment, including adjacent exhibits. Preserve any observed identifier without renumbering or imposing a maximum; do not infer exhibits from gaps.
PRECEDENCE: The complete decision directly challenged by the current Main Petition is Impugned Order when its court/authority, case number, date and decision type match the challenge/prayer and outer Index evidence, even if presented as Annexure P-X. Its annexure label is contextual identity, not the primary category. Background decisions remain Annexures.

categories.name: Application
categories.description:
IDENTITY: Each independent application/I.A. for incidental or procedural relief in the current Supreme Court proceeding.
START: Its own application title or I.A. identity, linked to a body requesting that relief. APPLICATION, I.A. and INTERLOCUTORY APPLICATION with clear OCR variants are cues; a caption alone is insufficient.
CONTINUE: Keep its pleadings, prayer, signature and affidavit expressly supporting that application together, even when the affidavit has a separate Supreme Court caption. Include captionless continuations and internal attachments unless independently established as outer exhibits/documents.
END: Before the next independently established current application or other outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: A citation such as 'Annexure P-X, Kindly see Pages ...' does not transfer the application's body or prayer into that exhibit. The attachment starts at its actual source opening, after the application's own closing pages. PRAYER, RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH/SHEWETH, a continued heading or an application-supporting affidavit does not start another segment. The primary substantive pleading is Main Petition. Lower-court applications and historical Supreme Court applications reproduced inside an Annexure stay enclosed, even with APPLICATION/I.A. headings or matching parties.
REPEAT: Separate adjacent applications must remain separate segments; each requires its own supported current-proceeding start.

categories.name: Appendix
categories.description:
IDENTITY: An independent appendix of the current Supreme Court paper book, commonly reproducing provisions, statutes, rules, regulations, notifications or schedules.
START: An outer APPENDIX, APPENDIX-I/II or numbered/lettered variant, including OCR variants such as APPENDlX, corroborated by outer filing context or a matched Index entry.
CONTINUE: Keep its complete reference material, schedules and continuations.
END: Before the next independently established appendix or other outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: A case-specific APPENDIX OF WP(C) listing PETITIONER/RESPONDENT EXHIBITS is integral to its reproduced judgment/record. Legal subject matter alone is insufficient. Legal text under an outer Annexure remains Annexures. An internal APPENDIX within a reproduced petition, judgment, application or record stays enclosed despite its own title page, pagination or court caption.
REPEAT: Each independently presented outer appendix starts a new segment.

categories.name: Memo of Parties
categories.description:
IDENTITY: A separately presented party list adopted as its own outer section of the current Supreme Court paper book.
START: MEMO OF PARTIES, MEMORANDUM OF PARTIES or a clear variant with party identities, addresses and procedural designations, supported by its independent outer presentation.
CONTINUE: Include all parties, addresses and continuation pages.
END: Before the next independently established outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: A party block within Main Petition, Application or an order belongs there. A separately indexed list may say BEFORE THE HIGH COURT; a lower-court caption alone does not exclude it. A memo inside a reproduced record/Annexure stays enclosed. MEMO OF JUDGMENT/JUDGEMENT qualifies only when it functions as this separately presented party list.
REPEAT: A distinct outer memo starts a new segment.

categories.name: Memo of Appearance
categories.description:
IDENTITY: An independent memo recording an advocate/AOR or party's appearance for a named party in the current Supreme Court proceeding.
START: MEMO OF APPEARANCE, MEMORANDUM OF APPEARANCE or a clear variant such as MEMO OF APPREARANCE, with an appearance statement and current proceeding context.
CONTINUE: Keep the memo's party details, date, signatures and captionless integral continuation.
END: Before the next independently established outer document, including a separately starting Vakalatnama.
DO NOT SPLIT: This records appearance rather than granting counsel authority. Lower-court appearance memos and historical Supreme Court memos reproduced inside an Annexure stay enclosed, even with an exact MEMO OF APPEARANCE heading or matching parties. A counsel/appearance list within an order or judgment remains in that record. When Memo of Appearance and Vakalatnama share one physical page, assign that page to Vakalatnama.
REPEAT: Each separately starting current-case memo on another page remains its own segment; adjacency to Vakalatnama alone does not combine them.

categories.name: Impugned Order
categories.description:
IDENTITY: The complete decision directly challenged by the current primary pleading, not a reference or quotation.
START: The actual decision copy, including its dedicated cover/caption, matched to the Main Petition's challenge/prayer and corroborating outer Index evidence by court/authority, case number, decision date and type. Strong agreement can tolerate one missing/OCR-damaged identifier; a generic heading or recency alone is insufficient.
CONTINUE: Include all party/appearance pages, judgment/order body, continuations, signatures and integral certification.
END: Before the next independently established outer document or separately presented challenged decision.
DO NOT SPLIT: Quotations inside Synopsis, chronology or pleadings remain there. Background/relied-upon decisions are Annexures when filed as exhibits. A challenged High Court/tribunal/lower-authority decision need not have a Supreme Court caption; do not require a Supreme Court caption.
REPEAT: Separately presented challenged decisions may form separate segments. Keep an explicitly continuous composite order-set together.
PRECEDENCE: A matched directly challenged decision remains Impugned Order even if its Index row, separator, cover or endorsement says Annexure P-X; preserve the exhibit identifier as context without returning invented metadata fields.

categories.name: Vakalatnama
categories.description:
IDENTITY: An independent instrument appointing counsel/AOR to act for a party in the current Supreme Court proceeding.
START: VAKALATNAMA, VAKALAT NAMA, VAKALTNAMA, V/A or a clear OCR variant, supported by appointment/authorization-of-counsel language and current proceeding context; an abbreviation or matching parties alone is insufficient.
CONTINUE: Include party signatures, counsel acceptance and captionless integral continuations.
END: Before the next independently established outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: Court-fee stamps do not change this category. Lower-court instruments and historical Supreme Court instruments reproduced inside an Annexure/Application stay enclosed, even with an exact VAKALATNAMA heading. A lower-court Memo of Appearance inside an annexure is not a current Vakalatnama. PoA/BR authorizes a representative and is a different function. If Memo of Appearance shares the same physical page, use Vakalatnama; a separately starting Memo of Appearance on another page remains separate.
REPEAT: A distinct current-proceeding appointment instrument starts a new segment.

categories.name: PoA/BR
categories.description:
IDENTITY: An independent Power of Attorney or Board Resolution establishing a representative's authority to act for a party in the current Supreme Court filing.
START: A principal/grantor empowering a representative, or corporate meeting/resolution language such as RESOLVED THAT authorizing proceedings. Match the represented party and purpose; a Supreme Court caption is not required.
CONTINUE: Include integral signatures, schedules, certification and continuations.
END: Before the next independently established outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: Generic power-to-act language or an advocate signature alone is insufficient. Distinguish counsel appointment under Vakalatnama and appearance recorded in Memo of Appearance. Instruments enclosed in an Annexure or another document stay there.
REPEAT: A separately presented authority instrument starts a new segment.

categories.name: Filing Memo
categories.description:
IDENTITY: An independent submission memo identifying papers being tendered in the current Supreme Court proceeding.
START: FILING MEMO, FILING INDEX, INDEX OF FILING or a clear variant, with a submission purpose and filing advocate/AOR, case particulars or filing date.
CONTINUE: Include the submission list, continuation sheets, date and signature.
END: Before the next independently established outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: Determine function rather than title: a contents table mapping paper-book documents to printed pages is Index, even if titled FILING INDEX. A filing-memo row in that table stays Index. A lower-court/reproduced memo stays with its enclosing record.
REPEAT: A separately presented submission memo starts a new segment.

categories.name: Court Fees
categories.description:
IDENTITY: An independent court-fee payment, stamp or endorsement sheet for the current Supreme Court filing.
START: A standalone sheet whose primary function is recording/evidencing court fees, supported by payment, stamp or fee-endorsement content and current filing context.
CONTINUE: Include the payment details and integral receipt/endorsement continuations.
END: Before the next independently established outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: Stamps, fee amounts or endorsements on Vakalatnama, Application, Cover Page or another document stay in that document. Index entries and Checklist responses about fees are not Court Fees. A reproduced lower-court fee sheet stays in its exhibit.
REPEAT: A separate outer fee document starts a new segment.

categories.name: Custody Certificate
categories.description:
IDENTITY: An independent jail/prison custody or surrender certificate relevant to the accused/convict/petitioner in the current criminal filing.
START: CUSTODY CERTIFICATE or a clear variant, with issuing-authority details and custody, sentence, surrender or release particulars. Match the person and underlying case where available; a Supreme Court caption is not required.
CONTINUE: Include all custody particulars, continuation sheets and issuing-authority certification.
END: Before the next independently established outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: Custody statements within a bail/suspension Application are not a separate certificate. A certificate inside a supported Annexure or Application package retains that enclosing category.
REPEAT: A separately presented outer certificate starts a new segment.

categories.name: Rejoinder
categories.description:
IDENTITY: A current-party pleading responding to an opposing counter-affidavit, reply or written response.
START: A separately presented REJOINDER or REJOINDER AFFIDAVIT with response content and current-case context.
CONTINUE: Keep its complete response, verification, signatures and integral annexures together.
END: Before the next independently established outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: A rejoinder mentioned in another document is not a boundary. A historical/lower-court rejoinder inside an Annexure stays enclosed. Do not confuse a respondent's counter-affidavit or reply with the petitioner's rejoinder.
REPEAT: Each separately filed response starts a separate segment. This category is optional and must not be inferred as present.

categories.name: Written Submissions
categories.description:
IDENTITY: A separately presented party/advocate memorandum of legal submissions for the current proceeding.
START: WRITTEN SUBMISSIONS, WRITTEN ARGUMENTS or equivalent heading with argument text, authorities or cited cases.
CONTINUE: Keep all argument pages, lists of authorities and integral schedules together.
END: Before the next independently established outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: A Synopsis, petition grounds, oral-hearing Record of Proceedings or submissions quoted inside a judgment are not Written Submissions. Historical submissions reproduced in an Annexure stay enclosed.
REPEAT: Separately filed sets remain separate. This category is optional and must not be inferred as present.

categories.name: Proof of Service
categories.description:
IDENTITY: An independently presented record proving service/delivery of current-case papers.
START: PROOF OF SERVICE, AFFIDAVIT OF SERVICE or an acknowledgment with recipient, served papers and delivery/service particulars.
CONTINUE: Keep an integral service affidavit, receipts, tracking and acknowledgments as one packet.
END: Before the next independently established outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: Service references or receipts inside an Application, Affidavit or Annexure stay there. Do not infer service from a mere statement.
REPEAT: Each independent service packet is separate. This category is optional and must not be inferred as present.

categories.name: Translation Certificate
categories.description:
IDENTITY: An independently presented translator/certifier statement authenticating a translation submitted in the current filing.
START: TRANSLATION CERTIFICATE, TRANSLATOR'S OATH/DECLARATION or equivalent with source document/language and translator/certifier details.
CONTINUE: Keep the certification, oath, signature and integral translator pages together.
END: Before the next independently established outer document.
DO NOT SPLIT: A certificate integral to a translation packet stays with that packet when no independent outer boundary exists. A translation mention or exemption Application is not a certificate. Historical certificates inside an Annexure stay enclosed.
REPEAT: Each separately presented certificate is separate. This category is optional and must not be inferred as present.

splitting_strategy.custom_instructions:
OUTPUT: Use only configured category names and physical PDF pages starting at 1; do not invent category names, numbered filenames or reason/metadata fields. Assign each page once; keep uncertain pages uncategorized. Categories are types, not document IDs: separately established documents need separate segments. Do not merge separate Memo of Appearance and Vakalatnama segments because of downstream UI grouping. Do not force optional categories to appear.

DECISION ORDER: (1) Establish the current outer filing and each supported outer document boundary. (2) Decide whether the page belongs to an already established document or enclosed packet. (3) Only then classify a new standalone document; use function, opening, body, case context and category descriptions' positive/negative cues. A heading, party name, caption, Index row, page-number reset or keyword alone never overrides established enclosure. When cues conflict, prefer coherent source/layout continuity and enclosing context over a title match; use an Index range only when corroborated by actual pages. Do not create a boundary merely to satisfy a category or expected filing order.

BOUNDARIES: Start at an independent opening supported by title/function and body, or by an outer Index range corroborated against actual pages. Dedicated title/party pages belong with their body. End before the next supported opening and retain complete closing material. Missing signatures, dates, attestation or case numbers do not mean absence. Do not enforce fixed document order/page counts or split within a physical page. If one page contains material from both sides of a boundary, assign it once to the document best supported by page function and layout; never duplicate or split a physical page.

CONTINUATION AND NESTING: Keep bodies, tables, verification, signatures and integral continuations together. Missing captions, pagination resets, quotations, PRAYER, TRUE COPY or mentions do not establish boundaries. Lower-court and historical Supreme Court records reproduced inside an Annexure stay enclosed despite exact category headings; internal documents in an Application stay with it. Apply the same enclosure rule to content reproduced within any established outer document unless a separately filed outer document is independently supported. A common judgment's connected-case captions and case-specific exhibit-list appendices remain in that same judgment. Captionless continuations inherit their established parent. Near-blank scanned pages stay with that parent when continuity supports this, but not across a new outer opening. Forms retain their own closing declarations, certificates and advocate details.

INDEX/FOLIOS: The outer Index is an inventory, not proof that listed documents exist. Reconnect OCR-separated rows only with layout/continuation support. Map printed folios to physical pages using evidence; covers, unnumbered/lettered pages, volumes and reproduced-record pagination change offsets. Do not extrapolate one offset across volumes; do not infer a missing annexure from a numbering gap (including an Annexure P-X gap); never give one document a whole gap shared by multiple unresolved Index rows. Stamps/source continuity can outweigh a conflicting Index range. A narrative page-range citation may corroborate the referenced opening but never starts an exhibit on its citing page.

OWNERSHIP/PRECEDENCE: Main Petition, Application, primary Affidavit, Record of Proceedings, Memo of Appearance and Vakalatnama belong to the current Supreme Court proceeding only when purpose, case identity and enclosing context support that ownership; matching parties or titles do not promote an earlier case's records. An application-supporting affidavit stays with its Application, even with a separate Supreme Court caption. A standalone Impugned Order can have the caption of the court/authority under challenge; classify it only when its case/date/decision matches the current Main Petition's challenge/prayer. Background judgments remain Annexures. Do not impose a Supreme Court caption on these or on Annexures. A court caption alone never establishes a category/boundary. For a combined SYNOPSIS AND LIST OF DATES heading, narrative pages are Synopsis and chronological pages are List of Dates & Events. Use AOR's Certificate function without a fixed heading-position requirement. If Vakalatnama and Memo of Appearance share one page, use Vakalatnama.
